stops.note: named the hardy root vegetable grown at extreme Andean altitudes
Inca farmers grew it at over 4,000 metres in the Junín plateau
stops.meaning: an Andean root crop grown at high altitude

stops.note: entered English through the global market for Andean 'superfoods'
stops.meaning: a nutrient-dense Andean root marketed as a health supplement

current_meaning: a hardy Andean root vegetable, dried and used as a nutritional supplement
